correctness.rationale: For a zero-free rank-two generator matrix with projective multiplicities \(m_i\), conditioning on the first projective class gives the exact identity \(\mathbb E=1+\sum_i m_i/(n-m_i)\). Zero columns are strictly dominated. The discrete first difference of \(f(t)=t/(n-t)\) is \(n/((n-t-1)(n-t))\), strictly increasing, so every imbalance of at least two is strictly improvable. This proves the balanced multiplicity formula and equality characterization. Exact exhaustive checks over \(2\le q\le6\) and \(2\le n\le10\) agree.
